items.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Mr. Wright, who was the road manager, then he’d come and he would sit up there, sit up there with him and then I could go take a nap.

ctx.x: Didn’t Calloway finally get a railroad car?

Well see Calloway’s band would be in the Cotton Club for six months. And then, they’d keep the same show in the Cotton Club for six months and then that show would travel for six months. And so we would go from here, you know, and stop, making all the little stops going down to the south, and that’s when he had a Pullman. He had this big Pullman with an extra car where all the musicians had their trunks. Milton and I, we always had lower seven berth, but then there was a car next to that, and you had your trunk,…

dressed and go out. Because that way it alleviated the necessity of having to try to find places to stay and we would go to California using the Pullman. And coming back — oh and I must say Cab had his big automobile on the car, on the Pullman, it was really nice. And then coming back we would hire, he would hire a Greyhound bus, a very nice bus. We were fortunate that we never had to travel in cars like most of the other musicians in those days. They had to pile in automobiles. But Calloway was first class all…
